New day, new question!

You've backed a kickstarter for a game/book/RPG, and got an alpha copy of it, Do you give it a good read or do you wait for the "proper" copy to make its way to you?

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: Wait for a proper copy

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
It depends. For example:

  • If they're asking for editorial feedback, I try to make time to provide it.
  • If I need it for a current RPG game (as has happened), I'll give it an initial read to determine what I'll be able to use at a high-level (and to make notes on things that I'll need answers to if they're missing from this version). 
  • If they're looking for playtesting feedback, I probably won't -- I can't make the time to playtest GTG and Handelabra's stuff as much as I'd like, and I have significant motivation there, so I won't be able to make time for any other playtesting.

posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
You're welcome. Turns out today has a high chance of being just as dreary, so I guess I'm staying inside.

If it's a system I'm REALLY interested in, then I'll probably give it a once over. but depending on how often they plan on releasing updated versions(The Savage Worlds Adventure edition book has had 3 updates in as many weeks!), I may just wait for the book proper before I give it a full read through. Or at least until the company decides to cool it on updates...

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
I usually wait for a proper copy before diving in. Unless it's something I really really want, then I start right away.
